named.name: Ammonolysis of alkyl halides
named.eq: CH3Br + excess NH3 -> CH3NH2 + HBr (further gives (CH3)2NH, (CH3)3N, (CH3)4NBr)
named.cond: Alkyl halide with excess ammonia, sealed tube, heat
named.tip: Examiners expect you to mention it gives a MIXTURE of primary, secondary, tertiary amine and quaternary ammonium salt, not just a clean primary amine.

named.name: Reduction of nitro compounds
named.cond: H2/Pd or H2/Ni (catalytic hydrogenation) or Sn/HCl followed by NaOH
named.tip: If Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl is used, remember a basification step with NaOH is needed afterward to liberate the free amine from its salt.

named.name: Reduction of nitriles
named.tip: Common mistake: writing the product with the same number of carbons as nitrile is correct here (CN carbon retained), unlike Hoffmann degradation.

named.name: Reduction of amides (Mendius reaction)
named.tip: Distinguish from Hoffmann bromamide degradation: LiAlH4 reduction of amide keeps the same carbon count, Hoffmann reduces carbon count by one.

named.name: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
named.eq: Phthalimide + KOH -> potassium phthalimide; + R-X -> N-alkylphthalimide; + hydrolysis (NaOH/H2O or H2NNH2) -> R-NH2
named.cond: KOH then alkyl halide, then hydrolysis (acid/alkaline hydrolysis)
named.tip: Key exam point: this method gives ONLY pure primary amine with no secondary/tertiary contamination; aromatic primary amines (Ar-NH2) CANNOT be prepared by this method.

named.name: Hoffmann bromamide degradation
named.tip: Product amine has ONE carbon LESS than the starting amide; this is frequently tested with a mechanism-based MCQ about migration of R group to nitrogen.

named.name: Diazotisation
named.cond: NaNO2 + dil. HCl (or H2SO4), 273-278 K (0-5 degree C)
named.tip: Always state the low temperature 273-278 K; above this the diazonium salt decomposes to phenol and N2.

named.name: Coupling reaction (azo dye formation)
named.cond: Weakly acidic/alkaline medium, cold, with aniline or phenol
named.tip: Azo coupling occurs mainly at the para position; with phenol the product is p-hydroxyazobenzene formed in weakly alkaline medium.

named.name: Carbylamine (isocyanide) reaction
named.tip: Positive test (foul smell) is given ONLY by primary amines (1 degree); secondary and tertiary amines give no reaction.

named.name: Hinsberg test reaction
named.eq: RNH2 + C6H5SO2Cl -> RNHSO2C6H5 + HCl (soluble in KOH); R2NH + C6H5SO2Cl -> R2NSO2C6H5 + HCl (insoluble in KOH)
named.tip: Explain the reason for solubility difference: primary amine product retains an acidic N-H (forms soluble K-salt), secondary amine product has no acidic N-H left.

steps: Alternative: C6H5NO2 + 3Sn/6HCl -> C6H5NH3+Cl- (then NaOH to liberate free amine)
conversions.ans: Catalytic hydrogenation (H2/Ni) or Sn/HCl followed by NaOH
Reduce the amide with LiAlH4 (same carbon count retained)

steps: Step 1: CH3CONH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH --(Hoffmann bromamide degradation)--> CH3NH2 + Na2CO3 + 2NaBr + 2H2O
conversions.ans: Hoffmann bromamide degradation (loses one carbon as CO2/carbonate)

conversions.q: Convert ethyl bromide (CH3CH2Br) to pure ethanamine (CH3CH2NH2) without secondary/tertiary contamination
steps: Step 2: Potassium phthalimide + CH3CH2Br -> N-ethylphthalimide + KBr
Step 3: N-ethylphthalimide + NaOH/H2O (hydrolysis) -> CH3CH2NH2 + phthalate salt
conversions.ans: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis gives pure primary amine, no over-alkylation

steps: Step 1: C6H5NH2 + NaNO2 + 2HCl --(273-278 K)--> C6H5N2Cl + NaCl + 2H2O (diazotisation)
Step 2: C6H5N2Cl + H2O --(warm, hydrolysis)--> C6H5OH + N2 + HCl
conversions.ans: Diazotise aniline at 0-5 degree C, then hydrolyse the diazonium salt by warming with water

steps: Step 1: C6H5NH2 + NaNO2 + 2HCl --(273-278 K)--> C6H5N2Cl + NaCl + 2H2O
Step 2: C6H5N2Cl + H3PO2 + H2O --(reduction, deamination)--> C6H6 + N2 + H3PO3 + HCl
conversions.ans: Diazotise then reduce with H3PO2/H2O to remove the amino group (deamination)

conversions.q: Convert aniline (C6H5NH2) to an azo dye (p-hydroxyazobenzene) using phenol
steps: Step 1: C6H5NH2 + NaNO2 + 2HCl --(273-278 K)--> C6H5N2Cl + NaCl + 2H2O
Step 2: C6H5N2Cl + C6H5OH --(weakly alkaline, cold)--> p-HO-C6H4-N=N-C6H5 + HCl
conversions.ans: Diazotise aniline, then couple with phenol in weakly alkaline solution at low temperature

conversions.q: Convert methyl bromide (CH3Br) to ethanamine (CH3CH2NH2) (one-carbon chain extension)
steps: Step 1: CH3Br + KCN -> CH3CN + KBr (nucleophilic substitution)
Step 2: CH3CN + 4[H] --(H2/Ni or LiAlH4)--> CH3CH2NH2 (reduction of nitrile)
conversions.ans: Convert the halide to nitrile with KCN, then reduce the nitrile (H2/Ni or LiAlH4) to get an amine with one more carbon
